resource.name: PM Pitfalls Self-Audit
resource.description: Twenty corpus-derived PM pitfalls. User rates each, gets back the three highest-leverage to fix this quarter with personalized narration.

tools.name: pm_pitfalls_get_questions
tools.description: Entry tool for the PM Pitfalls audit. Calling this triggers the host to mount the ui://working-from-lenny/pitfalls resource (an interactive iframe with the 20 questions, auto-advance, and submit). If your host mounts the UI, that IS the questionnaire — do NOT additionally render the 20 questions in chat as a duplicate surface; the user will answer in the iframe, which calls pm_pitfalls_score directly. The returned `questions` array is provided only as a fallback for hosts that cannot mount ui:// resources. Scoring is positional against this list — if you do render questions in chat (only when ui:// is unavailable), use these exact 20 verbatim; never substitute generic PM questions.

tools.name: pm_pitfalls_score
tools.description: Scores the user's PM-pitfalls audit and prepares their personalized narration brief. Returns the score (0-20), the three highest-leverage pitfall IDs, the pre-written exemplar quote per pick, and the canonical 20 questions. Answers are interpreted positionally against the canonical pitfalls — call pm_pitfalls_get_questions or render ui://working-from-lenny/pitfalls first; never substitute generic PM questions. AFTER receiving this score result, call pm_pitfalls_get_pending_narration to fetch the corpus-grounded narration brief, then render it for the user following its `directive` and `voice_rules`. Do not summarize the score on its own — the personalized narration is the user's deliverable. Optional `user_context` (role/stage/company size) flows into the persisted brief; pass it through if you have it. If the returned `persistence_warning` field is set, the brief could not be persisted — surface the warning to the user and recommend they retake the audit.

answers.description: Twenty answers in pitfall-ID order (1 through 20).

user_context.description: Optional. Role/stage/company-size context forwarded into the persisted narration brief's inputs.user_context for downstream rendering. Empty by default; iframe submission never sets one, chat-side Claude may.

exemplar_quotes.description: Pre-written corpus-anchored exemplar quote per top-three pitfall.

questions.description: Canonical 20 pitfall questions (id + text), echoed so the host has them in context for downstream rendering.

persistence_warning.description: Set only when score's persistence side-effect failed. Presence indicates pm_pitfalls_get_pending_narration will return no_pending for this audit and the host should surface the message to the user, recommending they retake.

tools.name: pm_pitfalls_narrate
tools.description: Packages a corpus-grounded narration brief for the user's top three pitfalls. Returns voice rules, structure, picks (pitfall text + exemplar quote + corpus anchors), and the corpus chunks themselves. Pure compute — no persistence side-effect. The host chat model renders the user-facing narration from this brief. To pick up the brief that score saved for the chat-side handoff, call pm_pitfalls_get_pending_narration instead.

user_context.description: Optional. User's role, stage, company size — sharpens the narration. Empty string if not provided.

answers.description: Optional. Pass through the user's 20 answers (in pitfall-id order) from the score call so the brief can ground specific behavioral claims in actual answers.

user_answer.description: Optional. Populated when narrate was called with the answers array.

full_audit.description: Optional. Per-pitfall user answer mapping. Present only when narrate was called with the answers array. Use to ground specific behavioral claims; do NOT invent answers when this field is absent.

corpus.description: Map of anchor slug to corpus chunk text.

tools.name: pm_pitfalls_get_pending_narration
tools.description: MUST CALL whenever the user asks for their PM Pitfalls 'personalized read', 'narration', 'audit results writeup', or any follow-up to an audit just taken — including any phrasing like 'narrate my pitfalls', 'give me my personalized read', 'show me my results', 'I completed the audit', or any message coming from the embedded widget. Do NOT respond with 'you haven't taken the audit' without calling this tool first: the audit state lives on disk (persisted by pm_pitfalls_score on submission), NOT in the chat conversation context — the user may have submitted via the embedded widget, in which case the chat history shows no prior audit-taking but a brief is waiting on disk. Returns the narration brief saved by the most recent pm_pitfalls_score call. On status='ready', render the brief following its directive and voice_rules. ONLY on status='no_pending' (meaning the disk check came back empty) direct the user to render the ui://working-from-lenny/pitfalls resource to take the audit.

tools.name: pm_pitfalls_drift
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Returns the user's calibration drift if they've audited before — what shifted, what didn't, and a one-line read. Stores audit answers locally across runs.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.phase_note: Web/URL-trick versions don't expose this tool. State requires the MCP App; host's confirmation UI handles the consent surface.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.comment: MCP resource spec for #44 PM Pitfalls Self-Audit. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. Validated against MCP Apps spec (Jan 2026 release + current draft) on 2026-05-18.

dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.summary: Narration tools in this app return a narration_brief, not the structured prose directly. The outputSchema(s) defined above describe the target rendering structure the host chat model is asked to produce. At runtime each narration tool returns { type: 'narration_brief', audience: 'user', directive, voice_rules, structure: { sections, per_section_template, length_cap }, inputs: <tool-specific>, corpus: { anchor_slug: chunk_text } }. The host chat model then renders the user-facing prose from the brief.
dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.worked_example: bundle/src/tools/pm-pitfalls/narrate.ts and bundle/src/shared/schemas.ts (PitfallNarrateOutput). Sonnet clones this pattern for every narration tool listed below.
dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.supersedes: Earlier 'host sampling + api_key fallback' design. Sampling/createMessage was not exposed by Claude Desktop or Claude Code CLI to user-installed extensions in 2026-05; Path 4 makes the host chat model the renderer, which is the MCP-recommended idiom.

dev.workingfromlenny.open_questions: Confirm enum-in-array works in MCP tool inputSchema.
Decide how pm_pitfalls_drift signals statefulness to the host.
dev.workingfromlenny.proposed_answers: Yes. MCP tool inputSchema follows JSON Schema (draft 7 subset). Enum constraints on array items are fully supported. The 'answers' field as specified is valid.

Use the tool-level annotations.readOnlyHint: false hint (now set above). The MCP Apps spec leaves consent UX to host discretion — there is no manifest-level requires-consent or data-retention flag. The host's confirmation UI handles per-call or install-time consent however that host chooses. Document persisted data in the tool description (answers array + timestamp per run) so the host's confirmation can convey it.

notes: ui:// scheme is valid; no rigid format is enforced — server-defined slugs after the scheme are acceptable.

No requires-consent / data-retention / fs-write capability exists in either ext-apps appCapabilities or .mcpb manifest. Consent is host-discretion; readOnlyHint: false on stateful tools is the only normative hook.
Underscore-prefixed fields at non-_meta paths have undefined host behavior; project metadata lives under _meta with reverse-DNS keys.
